source: YouTube auto-caption transcript 0:00-19:45 (tools/video_draft.py transcript kMo5X6G9lAU --start 0 --end 1170), card names corrected against data/Sets/FRA_PremierDraft_All_Data.json; nothing past 19:45 read. 'type' marks each idea as claim, heuristic or one-off pick; 'repeats' lists ideas of earlier videos it restates; 'related' lists looser topic matches. Solo draft: every idea is the host's (speaker field kept for the schema).

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Dark Matter Manipulator is a one-mana 3/2 a lot of the time because it is easy to reach seven cards with a free mill three, but it is worse than Plan for All Outcomes.
ideas.quote: It's like a one mana 3-2 a lot of the time because it's pretty easy to get to seven cards when you're spotting yourself a free mill three.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Dark Matter Manipulator against Plan for All Outcomes.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Plan for All Outcomes is a really strong kill spell that later lets you surveil on every noncreature spell, and works in blue-red, blue-white and blue-black Jace decks.
ideas.quote: This card's really strong as a kill spell that then eventually lets you surveil every time you play a non-creature spell.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Plan for All Outcomes by colour pair.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Blue is a good colour for Jace decks: blue-red uses Plan for All Outcomes well, blue-white because it cares about surveil, and blue-black.
ideas.quote: I do really like blue decks in this format. Blue Red uses this quite well. Blue White uses this quite well because it cares about surveilling.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate of blue pairs against others by skill.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Recursive Recruitment is one of the best win conditions at common or uncommon for a graveyard strategy, and easy to splash from blue-green; he takes it over Stingcaster Mage (a 2/1 that draws a card).
ideas.quote: It's one of the best like win conditions at common or uncommon for a graveyard strategy.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Recursive Recruitment against Stingcaster Mage.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: He has a rule to almost never pass Mindseeker Oculus: even if he were not blue-black, he could use it; he prefers it to Proft or Your Fate Ends Here even in a blue-white deck.
ideas.quote: I have a rule for myself and that's like almost never pass Mindseeker Oculus.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Mindseeker Oculus against Your Fate Ends Here and Proft.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Pair signals: when a pack still has both halves of a pair, nothing is missing and there is no information.
ideas.quote: I'm not getting any info from the pairings though because this pair is still here and this is half of a pair. So nothing's missing.
ideas.test_idea: How often a pack with all pair partners present predicts the upstream drafter's colours.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: The basic landcyclers are very playable, and the black one (Apex Witchstalker) especially so with Rewrite Regrets: cycle on turn two, get back the 6/4 menace on turn four.
ideas.quote: The cyclingers are very playable in this format. Like the black one is especially good to get back with this.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Rewrite Regrets by number of landcyclers; Apex Witchstalker win rate when cycled.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Twinned Vision is fine but not a card he wants more than one of; it is really good in the middle of the deck when he needs extra things to do.
ideas.quote: Twin vision fine, but not a card I ever really want more than one of.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Twinned Vision by copy count.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Extended Absence at pick five is a signal that black is open: it is the best black common and many uncommons were still in the pack, so few drafters upstream take black.
ideas.quote: Extended options pick five is I think a signal to some degree that black might be open.
ideas.test_idea: Whether Extended Absence arriving at pick 5 predicts black flow.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Apex Witchstalker is a good combo with Rewrite Regrets and a card he does not mind casting at the top of the curve; he takes it over Icy Reception, a card he has gone up and down on.
ideas.quote: I think this card's really a good combo with Rewrite Regrets and is also a card I don't mind casting at the top end of my curve.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Apex Witchstalker against Icy Reception.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: In a graveyard deck he would rather splash green than red: green has Hapatra and the landcyclers help.
ideas.quote: I would rather splash green than red. And so I'll just take this card.
ideas.test_idea: Splash win rate by colour for blue-black graveyard decks.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: A wheeled card is value: Dark Matter Manipulator wheeled from the first pick, and the Charm and the land wheeled in pack two; when you think a card can wheel, take the one that cannot.
ideas.quote: When you think you can wheel cards, you get so much value.
ideas.test_idea: Wheel rate of gold uncommons in blue-black.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Seasoned Cryomancer (mythic) over Theorix Charm: he would take the charm without a mythic that fits; he expects a Charm to wheel because nobody else is blue-black.
ideas.quote: I would definitely take the charm if there wasn't a mythic rare that really fits my strategy well.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Seasoned Cryomancer against Theorix Charm.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Countersculpt is perfect for his control deck even with few Jace cards; he keeps taking it, because his deck wants the late game.
ideas.quote: I think I'm just going to keep taking counter sculpts. It's a really strong card.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Countersculpt by number of Jace cards in the deck.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Take the instant-speed kill spell for the deck over a good two-drop: Last Gasp over Proft, Consulting Detective.
ideas.quote: I just need the kill spell, especially instant speed makes it...
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Last Gasp against Proft, Consulting Detective.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Proft, Sinister Mastermind is an easy pick: the minus three minus one kills a lot of creatures and he can use it as a one-drop.
ideas.quote: Prof minus three minus one kills a lot of creatures in this format.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Proft, Sinister Mastermind.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: One copy of Theoretical Necromancer is fine in a deck that mills itself; he never wants a second one.
ideas.quote: I do like one copy of the necromancer in these decks if I'm milling myself.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Theoretical Necromancer by copy count.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: He only ever wants one Unsummon in this type of deck, so he takes Gallia, Tragic Host (fits the mill plan, a two-drop that can come back) over it.
ideas.quote: I only ever want one unsummon in this type of deck.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate of Unsummon by copy count in UB.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Infinite Coursework is honestly a marginal card but still makes his deck as an unconditional kill spell for many things.
ideas.quote: Infinite coursework is honestly a card that's more marginal, but I still think it's going to make the cut.
ideas.test_idea: Main-deck rate and GIH WR of Infinite Coursework.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Take a land for consistency when you will have many playables: Theorix Annex over Fblthp, Impossibly Lost, which is not as good in a deck not going hard on mill.
ideas.quote: Getting a land to make my mana more consistent is going to be a really nice thing to have here.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Theorix Annex in blue-black decks.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Rank Rat is better than Tetsuko for a deck with one Mindseeker Oculus: the Rat trades with the opponent's resources, Tetsuko is an aggressive card.
ideas.quote: Rat at least does a little bit of trading with their resources which we care about.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Rank Rat against Tetsuko Umezawa, Fugitive.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: 17 lands with two eight-drops that are pretty good; he considers cutting a land because the landcyclers are break-in-case-of-emergency lands.
ideas.quote: I think this is a 17 land deck. We have two eight drops that are pretty dang good.
ideas.test_idea: Land count against win rate in blue-black graveyard decks with landcyclers.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Cut Teyo, Keeper of the Quiet Hour, Necromancer and Afterthought Sentry; keep Theorix Metamage for the graveyard (milling it makes it a 3/2), Fblthp over Divining Duelist is the close call.
ideas.quote: Theorix Metamage is probably better just for graveyard synergy stuff. Like milling one of these is really good.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Theorix Metamage by self-mill count.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: The mana wants equal numbers of both colours: lots of cheap black cards early but also double-blue cards; so he plays eight Island and eight Swamp with one dual.
ideas.quote: We want to have equals of both because we have a lot of black cards early, but also double blue cards.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate of UB decks by source split.
